subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should an ignore file above 4 MiB terminally exclude its entire subtree, including overriding other ignore-file negations in that directory?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but choosing between secret-safe fail-closed behavior and preserving existing workspace discovery changes the security and compatibility contract for all scan callers.

options.title: Approve terminal fail-closed
options.body: Accept the 4 MiB limit and whole-subtree exclusion as the security-first contract, preferably with a visible oversized-file diagnostic.

options.title: Preserve discovery compatibility
options.body: Skip only the oversized file and continue processing other ignore files, accepting that exclusions from the unread file cannot be enforced.

options.title: Require a diagnostic redesign
options.body: Pause landing until the shared API can return a structured oversized-policy outcome that every scanner can surface to users.

recommendation.title: Approve terminal fail-closed
recommendation.body: Accept the 4 MiB limit and whole-subtree exclusion as the security-first contract, preferably with a visible oversized-file diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice establishes a cross-cutting core workspace-scan compatibility and security policy rather than a file-local implementation detail.
